expectation: Cytoplasmic keratin filling epithelial/carcinoma cells, absent from stroma, immune and endothelium. Common here: continuous bright sheets and gland/crypt linings, with clear contrast against stroma and none off the tissue.
notes: Strong yellow haze and glare fill the slide off the tissue. The glandular epithelium in C is no brighter than its surroundings, and the brightest 'cell' (D) lies off the tissue. Bright spots are blobs not tied to cells, and Ecadherin is empty, so row E tells us nothing.
observed: A: haze and glow bands over the whole slide, including off-tissue; the tissue shows only faint grainy yellow. B: haze and scattered blobs. C: gland ring not lit, with a thin rim and bright debris in and around it. D: blobs, off-tissue. E: irregular specks; Ecadherin shows no cells.
why: No epithelial population lights up above haze, glare and debris; the epithelium seen in C is unstained and the brightest objects lie off the tissue.
